analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It adds a paragraph at head lines 253-259 saying the SSD prefix-cache staging runs before engine.submit, off the engine queue. It says provider-staged complete-checkpoint imports create their destinations already available from host bytes and never evaluate or fence them, so staging does not wait on the MLX evalLock. It adds no executable code and changes no controls, so there is no direct security regression. The sentence describes a change that presumably lives in CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, which was not supplied. Review there should confirm that host-byte imports still authenticate the payload before it is trusted. That means AES-GCM with AAD/context binding, HMAC lookup tag and cacheSalt scoping, the weightHash/layoutEpoch bindings, and release of the shared GlobalKVCacheBudget staging reservation on failure. This matters for T-041 (A-001 cache confidentiality and integrity, SEC-035) and for availability under T-029. The description is that staging creates destinations without a fence or evaluation, which could affect memory-ordering or lifetime safety. That claim cannot be verified from this evidence. It does not affect T-041's mitigations as documented (HMAC-keyed names, TTL, authenticated account scoping). The T-041 threat-model entry does not need updating from this docs-only change. The other content (MiMo, Qwen4, calibration) appears as unchanged context. No unchanged callers were examined, and the linked ssd-kv-cache.md reference was not supplied.
